sections.name: component-level 4D (part 1)
sections.title: Component-level timeline checks
sections.what: Runs checks that a component goes from future to active to complete, that events are sorted and unique, that next and previous navigation stops at the ends, that missing baseline dates are not replaced with planned dates, and that partial actual dates do not invent completion.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are the rules most likely to show wrong work status to a user.
sections.watch_out: The baseline check expects planned dates never to fill in for missing baseline dates, so changing that fallback breaks it on purpose.

summary: Checks the 4D timeline rules: whether a component is future, active or complete on a given date, how timeline event dates are sorted and de-duplicated, and how baseline and actual dates are handled.
purpose: Protects the timeline logic that drives the schedule playback in the viewer.
why: Likely reason: the timeline decides what the user sees at each date, so its rules are checked directly.
how: Builds a sample component and project, then runs checks in groups: state over time, event list, next and previous navigation, missing baseline dates, and partial actual dates.
inputs: Sample component and project data written in the file, and dates.
outputs: Pass or fail for each check.
risks: The checks use fixed sample dates. Edge cases outside those samples are not covered.
debug: If a check fails, compare the expected state or date in the test with what the timeline functions return for the same sample.
